body:
## Summary
- add a PR workflow that uploads aliased Cloudflare Worker preview versions with Wrangler
- enable Worker preview URLs in Wrangler config and document required GitHub configuration
- add a guard test so the workflow does not regress to production deploys

## Test Plan
- [x] node --test tests/preview_workflow.test.js
- [x] ruby -e 'require \"yaml\"; YAML.load_file(\".github/workflows/pr-preview.yml\"); puts \"yaml ok\"'
- [x] git diff --check -- .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml wrangler.toml README.md tests/preview_workflow.test.js
- [x] CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_SUBDOMAIN=example-subdomain bash -lc 'worker=\"$(node -e '\''const fs = require(\"fs\"); const text = fs.readFileSync(\"wrangler.toml\", \"utf8\"); const match = text.match(/^name\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"/m); if (!match) process.exit(1); console.log(match[1]);'\'')\"; alias=\"pr-123\"; url=\"https://${alias}-${worker}.${CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_SUBDOMAIN}.workers.dev\"; echo \"$url\"'
- [x] npm run check
- [x] npm run check:wasm
- [x] npx wrangler versions upload --preview-alias codex-preview --message \"Local validation preview for PR preview workflow 4068869\"
- [x] npx wrangler versions view 2e47d3df-8cda-4801-88d2-3a6828f336e8 --json

## Notes
- The local Wrangler validation uploaded Worker version 2e47d3df-8cda-4801-88d2-3a6828f336e8 with alias codex-preview and did not deploy production traffic.
- Configure CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_SUBDOMAIN as a repository variable or secret so the workflow can comment deterministic preview URLs.

title: feat: badges page parity (relays, edit, naddr, follow-awardees)
body:
## Summary

Implements the full [badges-page-parity plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-badges-page-parity.md) in 20 commits. Closes the remaining gaps against `verbiricha/badges` while keeping Divine the default issuer, profile source, media host, and relay.

- **Relay read/write split**: marker-aware `relayUrlsFromRelayListEvent`, `discoverWriteRelays`, `relayPublishMany` (partial-success aware), `relayQueryManyDetailed` (per-relay `ok`/`error`).
- **Shared publish flow**: `publishSignedToWriteRelays` signs once, publishes to discovered write relays + `DIVINE_RELAY` + local `/relays` overrides. Every write flow (create / edit / award / accept / hide / follow-awardees / relay-list) routes through it.
- **Canonical naddr**: NIP-19 `encodeNaddr` with TLV type 1 relay hints, matches a live `nostr-tools` fixture. `/b/:naddr` is the default; raw `kind:pubkey:d` URLs still resolve.
- **Collection state on `/b/:coord`**: logged-in viewers see accept / hide / awarded / not-awarded with shared-helper publishing.
- **Owner edit flow**: `/b/:coord/edit` route + page; `buildEditedBadgeDefinitionEvent` preserves `d` and rebuilds replaceable metadata. Route is classified before the generic `/b/` route.
- **Relay settings at `/relays`**: discovered NIP-65 + local overrides (`ws://`/`wss://`), `kind:10002` publish via shared helper, per-relay connectivity check.
- **Nostr profile fallback**: `loadCreatorProfile` merges Divine API + `kind:0` metadata; awardee cards and issuer lookups no longer go blank for non-Divine users.
- **Safe markdown for descriptions**: paragraphs, line breaks, bold, inline code, safe `http(s)` links only. `javascript:` / `data:` stripped. Names, NIP-05s, relay URLs stay plain escaped.
- **Follow awardees**: `kind:3` contact-list merge from a badge detail page; preserves existing follows and content.
- **Created-tab owner actions**: view / award / edit / copy link on `/me` and owner-of `/p/:id`.

## Replaceable-event data-loss guard (flagged during review)

Final code review caught that `kind:30008` accept/hide and `kind:10002` publish weren't applying the "fetch before replace" invariant stated at plan line 113. Fixed in `8602936`:

- `buildAcceptProfileBadgesEvent` / `buildHideProfileBadgesEvent` now throw on `null`/`undefined` `profileEvent`.
- `me.js` / `profile.js` / `badge.js` switched to `relayQueryManyDetailed` and track `profileBadgesStatus: "unknown" | "empty" | "loaded"`. Refuse to publish when `"unknown"` (no read relay responded `ok`).
- `/relays` applies the same three-state classification to its published relay-list fetch.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test assets/app/**/*.test.js` — 133 tests green (10 spec files)
- [x] `npm run check` (`cargo fmt --check && cargo test --lib --tests`) — green
- [x] `npm run check:wasm` (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`) — green
- [x] naddr encoding matches `nostr-tools` fixture (committed in `identity.test.js`)
- [x] Route classification tested in `tests/landing_page_tests.rs` — edit route before generic badge route
- [ ] Manual browser checklist (required before deploy):
  - [ ] `/me` signed in + signed out
  - [ ] `/new` creates badge, uploads to `media.divine.video`, redirects to `/b/:naddr?award=1`
  - [ ] Owner can award on `/b/:naddr`
  - [ ] Recipient can accept/hide from `/me`
  - [ ] Recipient can accept/hide from `/b/:naddr`
  - [ ] Owner can edit on `/b/:naddr/edit`
  - [ ] `/relays` shows discovered + local, publishes `kind:10002`, per-relay check
  - [ ] Non-Divine Nostr users show profile metadata fallback
  - [ ] Created tab has view/award/edit/share actions
  - [ ] Raw coordinate URLs still load
  - [ ] Follow-awardees publishes a `kind:3` merge (does not wipe existing follows)

## Follow-ups (not blocking)

- Cache-buster version drift across imports — some modules imported at two different `?v=` versions from different views; unify in a cleanup pass.
- Untracked screenshots (`.playwright-mcp/`, `new-page-logged-out.png`, etc.) — either add to `.gitignore` or land intentionally.
